reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about the effects of vanadium on solid solution homogeneity, grain refinement, defect mobility, segregation tendencies, and radiation tolerance in W-Ta alloys, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises.
premises: Increasing V to 5 at.% promotes a more homogeneous BCC solid solution in W-Ta alloys.
Increasing V to 5 at.% induces grain refinement in nanocrystalline W-Ta films.
Higher V content lowers self-interstitial mobility relative to the W-Ta matrix and brings vacancy and interstitial mobilities closer together.
Higher V content weakens ordering/segregation tendencies, reducing irradiation-induced W enrichment and Ta depletion at grain boundaries.
The combined effects of V addition enhance defect recombination and limit void formation under irradiation.
